comments.author: @aldolopez1978
comments.text:
I am Spanish and I can confirm that several of this guy's claims are utter nonsense born of profound ignorance:
1) First of all, the Visigoths were not Germanic pagans. They adhered to the Arian heresy, as did a huge portion of Christendom at the time (including numerous bishops—see the Council of Nicaea). From 410 to 580, the Visigothic kings were Arianism. From 580 to 711, they were Catholic. However, it is important to note that only the rulers were Visigothic and Arian; the general population remained Hispanic and predominantly Catholic. There is a difference in northwestern Spain. Instead of Iberians, the people there were Celts. And instead of Visigoths, the Suebi arrived in the 5th century. The Suebi were pagans, but they converted to Catholicism 80 years later. The Kingdom of the Suebi was the first kingdom in Western Europe to adopt Catholicism as its official religion.
2) The Reconquista was not carried out by European peoples arriving from abroad; that is an incredibly stupid idea. The Reconquista was undertaken solely by the local Hispanic population—which explains why it was a slow process, as repopulation was required. Spain's ethnic makeup is far more homogeneous than that of the rest of Europe. Meanwhile, other Europeans were busy with their failed Crusades. The Reconquista began in 711, but by the year 1000, it had already reached the Duero River (covering one-third of the peninsula). In 1085, the former Visigothic capital of Toledo (south of Madrid) was reconquered. Córdoba (the former Muslim capital) was retaken in 1236, followed by Seville in 1248 and Cádiz in 1262, placing almost the entire territory in Christian hands with the sole exception of Granada, Málaga, and Almería. Furthermore, the idea that the Muslims were more advanced is a myth. They did nothing but copy what existed in the territories they conquered (Syria, Byzantium and Egypt, which were Christian). Visigothic Spain was the most culturally advanced region in western Europe at the time, and they took advantage of that.
3) The lack of population on the Meseta (an area much larger than what was indicated) is not due to Franco. In fact, the highest percentage of people living in that interior region was during the Franco era; indeed, it was Franco who built reservoirs to supply water. The population had always been sparse—firstly because the terrain is very challenging, and secondly due to the nature of the repopulation process during the Reconquista. Spain's entire coastal zone is extremely fertile, as are several areas along the major rivers. The interior, with altitudes of 1,000 meters, is a very harsh environment.
